sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: The aim of this document is to describe the web service RFX in terms of “what is it” and “how to use it”. It describes the webservice data-model, supported operations and related behavior and available interfaces.
Before going deeper with specific features of this webservice please ensure to review the document “J1P WS Development_Kit – Web Services Overview” which applies to all webservices.
The structure of the current document is the following:
1. Import/Update RfX method

2. Request data format: describes the possible operations on import (CREATE, UPDATE, CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE and so on) and describes the structure of the request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory depending on the operation you want to perform and those that can be omitted.
3. Behavior: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some particular processes.
4. Response data format: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes.
5. Export RfX method
6. Component Filters: describes which sections of an Rfx can be exported. The use of a component filter increments the number of sections in the response to every Rfx exported.
7. Condition Filters: describes which fields can be used to filter the Rfx to be extracted on specific conditions. So, the use of a condition filter allows to decrease the number of Rfx extracted.
8. Data Elements Condition Filters: describes how to filter on the data elements in order to retrieve only rfx having data elements with specific values.
9. Export Response data format: describes the structure of the response in terms of exported fields and sections.
10. Error codes: contains a list of possible error codes.
11. REST INTERFACE
12. Operation and Endpoints: describes REST available collections. Allowed calls with allowed parameters and supported HTTP methods
13. Request samples: contains detailed samples of HTTP request/response for each available operation
14. PUSH INTERFACE
15. Data model: refers to push message data format
16. Push Message samples: contains samples of push message

17. Data Types and UI Default Labels: describes the type of the fields and the corresponding label in English language in the platform with the aim to simplify the mapping between the fields visible in the platform and the fields used in the web service.

sections.title: Import/Update RfX method
paragraphs: This web service method can be used to import RfX into the JA platform. It implements creation of new item, update of existing one and “insert-update” logics (if an RfX with the given code/id already exists then the existing object is updated, otherwise a new element is created). Such behavior is ruled explicitly by providing in request a proper operation code.

sections.title: Existing RfX selection
paragraphs: When updating an existing RfX:
1. if rfxReferenceCode is provided but reference code service is not available, error is prepared to be returned.

2. Otherwise an RfX internal identifier matching such rfxReferenceCode is looked for: if no existing RfX can be found with such reference code or if rfxId value has been provided but such value doesn’t match that retrieved via rfxReferenceCode, error is returned.

3. RfX (with internal identifier provided or that retrieved by reference code) is then loaded and all updates act on such element (if RfX not found or if retrieved object doesn’t belong to calling instance web service is called on, error is returned).
When creating a new RfX:
1. rfxId field is never used;

2. if reference code service state reference code must manually be provided by user), a not empty value must be provided for rfxReferenceCode and this not-trimmed value must be unique over all the negotiation (deleted ones included), otherwise error is returned to caller.
3. If reference code service isn’t active or reference code is automatic, rfxReferenceCode value isn’t used.

sections.title: Creator/Updater Account Id Selection
paragraphs: When creating a new RfX, the web service tries to identify RfX owner as follows:
1. If companyData.id field is provided, it uses this account identifier to find out buyer company
2. If companyData.code field has been provided, it is used as the external code of the company to be found
3. if both field provided, it checks company retrieved via external code has the same identifier as companyData.code.

4. If no ownerUser data provided, the owner is retrieved company super user; otherwise it searches for the user in provided company having internal identifier or external code or login equal to ownerUser.id or ownerUser.code or ownerUser.login (if all three are provided, they must identify the same user)
When updating an existing object, the company web service operates with the same that initially created it.

If company is found, it also checks web service configuration to verify this company is granted with the possibility to operate and, if enabled, it selects company super user as the account requesting operation.
All specific permission and RfX configuration used to verify the validity of the request itself are then checked against this user.

sections.title: Tender (Project) selection
paragraphs: In case of creation of a new RfX, system needs to know the project item will be inserted in.

sections.title: Case when autoCreateTender = 0 (i.e. no request for project automatic creation)
paragraphs: At least one between tenderCode and tenderReferenceCode fields must be specified, must be not empty and must identify a project belonging to the same instance web service is called on.
If both fields are expressed, check is performed that the internal identifier of the project retrieved via tenderReferenceCode has the same value of provided tenderCode.

sections.title: Case when autoCreateTender = 1
paragraphs: A new project is automatically created with:
1. project title = short description of the RfX
2. project owner = superuser of the buyer company the RfX is associated to (it is possible to set a configuration parameter in order to assign the RfX owner as project owner)
3. RFQ Behavior in project = Independent RFQs

sections.title: Case when autoCreateTender = 2
paragraphs: A new project is automatically created with:
1. project title = short description of the RfX
2. project owner = superuser of the buyer company the RfX is associated to (it is possible to set a configuration parameter in order to assign the RfX owner as project owner)
3. RFQ Behavior in project = Multi-Lot RFQs
The new RfX just generated is then linked to the new project created.
When updating an existing RfX, these fields are ignored (no tender retrieval is needed).

sections.title: RfX template selection
paragraphs: In case of creation of a new RfX from a provided template, system needs to know the RfX template to inherit information from.
So, at least one between templateId and templateReferenceCode fields must be specified, must be not empty and must identify a template belonging to the same instance web service is called on.
If both fields are expressed, check is performed that the internal identifier of the template retrieved via templateReferenceCode has the same value of provided templateId.
When executing any other operation, these fields are ignored (no template retrieval is needed).

sections.title: Category Management
paragraphs: RfxCategoryList sub element is optional: that means that if this information is not provided, eVm classification of the RfX is not changed (newly created RfX is not classified or existing RfX classification is kept).
If this element is provided, the underlying category array (categoryList.getCategory()) is verified:

1. Category array hasn’t been defined (null value) or it has been defined (not null value) but it doesn’t contain any category: if operation is called in RESET mode, all previously associated categories are removed and RfX becomes unclassified.

Category array contains at least one category: web service ensures currently provided categories (identified via their code field) remain set for the RFx, while not listed categories are removed if operation is called in RESET mode, remains unchanged otherwise.

sections.title: Data Element Management
paragraphs: RfxAdditionalInfoList sub element is optional: that means that if this information is not provided, RfX data elements are not affected (newly created RfX has no additional info or existing RfX data elements are not changed).
If this element is provided, the underlying additional info array (rfxAdditionalInfoList.getAdditionalInfo()) is verified:

1. Additional Info array hasn’t been defined (null value) or it has been defined (not null value) but it doesn’t contain any additional info: if operation is called in RESET mode, all previously associated data elements are removed

2. Additional Info array contains at least one element: web service ensures currently provided data elements (identified by the value retrieved via provided data element name field) are created or updated, while not listed existing element are removed if operation is called in RESET mode, remains unchanged otherwise.

3. Updating the RFQ Award Type data element values does work as part of an UPDATE request, but only if the RFQ is in “to be published” or “running” statuses. If the RFQ is in a state where you can update the data element values associated with the RFQ Type on the “Settings” page, then you can successfully also update the data element values for the RFQ Award Type. The problem comes in once the RFQ transitions past RUNNING status. After that point, the web services are assuming that no updates of any kind can be made to the RFQ, because the RFX web service does not manage changes to the award details or evaluation data. RFX web service should allow the RFQ Award Type data element values to be updated in at least some statuses past RUNNING.

4. The request that is sent to update the RFQ Award Type data elements after the RFQ has moved past RUNNING status should be sent with an operation code of:UPDATE_ADDINFO instead of UPDATE. After an RFQ has moved past RUNNING status, any attempt to use the operation code of UPDATE will still fail.
5. As noted previously by Luca, any attempt to update data elements that are part of the RFQ Award Type should be in the awardRfxAdditionalInfoList parameter when sent in the request

6. The web service implementation needs to add a check and a more informative error message when processing an UPDATE_ADDINFO request if the request includes updates for the data elements of the RFQ Type if the RFQ is in a status after RUNNING (if this is attempted right now, the web service just responds with the same, not very informative error message we are seeing now).

7. Web service implementation should also check and provide the same, more informative error message if the RFQ is after RUNNING status and the operation code on import is anything other than UPDATE_ADDINFO (after RUNNING status, this is the only valid operation code for import).
8. Web service implementation will also check and provide the same, more informative error message if the RFQ is AWARDED status or later.

9. Web service implementation needs to be updated so that the UPDATE_ADDINFO operation code will handle updates to both the RFQ type data elements and the RFQ Award Type data elements (right now, UPDATE_ADDINFO only tries to save updates to the RFQ Type data elements).

sections.title: Attachment Management
paragraphs: BuyerAttachmentsList and SellerAttachmentsList sub-element are optional: that means that if an attachment list object is not provided, corresponding attachment structure is not changed.
If attachment container is provided, the underlying attachment array is verified:

1. Attachment array hasn’t been defined (null value) or it has been defined (not null value) but it doesn’t contain any attachment: if operation is called in RESET mode, RFx status is verified so that:
2. if the RFX is in DRAFT status, all existing attachments are deleted
3. if the RFX status is RUNNING (or following status) an error is returned
If operation is called in normal CREATE/UPDATE mode, attachment structure is unchanged.
1. Attachment array contains at least one element. If operation is called in RESET mode, RFx status is checked so that:
2. if the RFX is in DRAFT status, all existing attachments are deleted and replaced with the ones provided in the call
3. if the RFX status is RUNNING (or following status), an error is returned
If operation is called in normal CREATE/UPDATE mode, RFx status is still checked so that
1. if the RFX is in DRAFT status, the attachment is added or replaced according to the name (if an attachment with the same filename exists the uploaded one replaces the existing one)
2. if the RFX status is RUNNING (or following status) only new attachments are allowed, and so if an attachment with the same name already exists an error is returned.
3. Seller Attachments cannot be added to an Rfq in a state after RUNNING state.

sections.title: Envelope Management
paragraphs: TechEnvelope, QualEnvelope and CommEnvelope sub elements are optional: that means that if an envelope object is not provided, corresponding RfX envelope is not changed (newly created RfX hasn’t such envelope or previous envelope structure is not modified).
For each envelope, if the proper object container is provided, the underlying section array (envelope.getSection()) is verified:

1. Section array hasn’t been defined (null value) or it has been defined (not null value) but it doesn’t contain any section: if operation is called in RESET mode, all previously defined envelope sections are removed.

2. Section array contains at least one element: newly listed sections –section whose name can’t be found in existing section list- are inserted. If operation is called in RESET mode, web service ensures only currently provided sections (identified by their name field –case sensitive check-) remain for the RFx (not listed sections are removed);

For what concern section structure, an analogous mechanism has been implemented for parameter (and commercial envelope additional column) management. In particular, the parameter container (parameterList element) is always mandatory while commercial envelope additional column container (additionalColumnList) is optional. So:
1. If additionalColumnList object is not defined, commercial envelope additional column structure is not changed

2. Nor parameter neither additional column element is provided: if operation is called in RESET mode all corresponding section information is cleared, otherwise existing parameter or multi column data structure is kept

3. The array contains at least one object: web service will update elements having a valid id field and will create new object for the other (if operation is called in RESET mode, all existing item not listed are removed).

In particular, if the id field is provided, it must identify an existing parameter in the envelope we are working on, otherwise an error is returned and the operation abandoned: that means if we are totally creating new section for an envelope or if we want to create new parameter in an existing envelope section, the id field must not be provided (or provided with value -1 for commercial envelope additional column).

More, envelopes offer a further mechanism to update existing parameter or additional column on existing section. If the id field is not provided but it is provided the paramPos, enclosing section is searched for a parameter at such position. If not found (paramPos is not positive or it is greater than existing parameter number), an attempt is made to identify the parameter to update via the reference field: enclosing section is searched for a commercial parameter having such value for reference code.
If a parameter is found (via id, paramPos or reference), it will be updated otherwise a new parameter will be created.

For commercial envelope additional column, if the id field is not provided, it first check if columnPos has been provided and, when positive, if it is no greater than the actual number of additional parameter. If this is the case, actual parameter will be updated. Otherwise, the name value is checked to verify if a parameter exists with the same column title. Again, if a match is found, the corresponding parameter will be updated. In all other case, a new parameter will be added.
If a new TCO column is to be created with an existing TCO column, then the existing TCO column is automatically changed to be non-TCO with its TCO aggregate type cleared.
If more than one TCO columns are to be created, then only the first one will be created as TCO column, the rest will be created as non_TCO with title being kept but without aggregate type.
Formula details for the Numeric Single Row Formula type (formula value field) cannot be managed via the web services at this time.
Once a column is created, it’s type and columnUniqueCode are not allowed to be changed.
When creating a new additional column, if columnUniqueCode is provided in request, then it must be unique and not used by other existing additional columns within the same section.

sections.title: Supplier Management
paragraphs: SupplierList sub element is optional: that means that if this information is not provided, RfX supplier list is not changed (newly created RfX has no invited supplier or currently invited supplier list is not modified).
If this element is provided, the underlying supplier array (supplierList.getSupplier()) is verified:

1. Supplier array hasn’t been defined (null value) or it has been defined (not null value) but it doesn’t contain any supplier: if operation is called in RESET mode, all previously invited suppliers are removed, otherwise no operation is performed.

2. Supplier array contains at least one element: newly listed supplier (suppliers are identified by their companyData/[id|code|extUniqueCode] field) are inserted and, if operation is called in RESET mode, not listed supplier are removed.

sections.title: Evaluation Group Management
paragraphs: EvaluationGroupList sub element is optional: that means that if this information is not provided, RfX evaluation group list is not changed (newly created RfX has no evaluation group members or currently evaluation group list is not modified).
If this element is provided, the underlying evaluation group array is verified:

1. EvaluationGroup array hasn’t been defined (null value) or it has been defined (not null value) but it doesn’t contain any evaluation group: if operation is called in RESET mode, all previously evaluation groups are removed, otherwise no operation is performed.
2. EvaluationGroup array contains at least one element: newly listed evaluation groups are inserted and, if operation is called in RESET mode, not listed evaluation groups are removed.
EvaluationGroup without EvaluationGroupMember will be rejected.
EvaluationGroupMember without EvaluationUser will be rejected.

EvaluationGroupMember contains the optional PermissionList sub element. The sub element ForceRfxVisibility can redefine the permission by assigning the visibility on the Rfx for the evaluation user. If the permission is already present in the standard permissions, no redefinition is performed. If the permission is redefined for a user and the user is removed from the evaluation group, the permission (forced) persists. If you need to remove it, you can do it manually, from the platform. The ForceSensitiveDataVisibility permission follows the same logic.

sections.title: RfX Type Management
paragraphs: If a list of RfX Types is present, when a new RfX is created the RfX Type becomes mandatory.
If the RfX Type is not provided and a default Type exists, the default Type is associated to the new RfX.
If the RfX Type is not provided and there is not a default Type, an error is returned.
When an existing RfX is updated, if the RfX Type is not provided, the existing RfX Type is preserved.
If the RfX Type is provided it can be updated only if the RfX is not published yet.
In both cases (create, update), if the RfX Type is provided but no existing Type can be found with such code, an error is returned.

sections.title: Opening Committee Management
paragraphs: OpeningCommitteeList sub element is optional: that means that if this information is not provided, RfX opening committees list is not changed (newly created RfX has no opening committees members or currently opening committees list is not modified).
If this element is provided, the underlying opening committees array is verified:

1. OpeningCommittee array hasn’t been defined (null value) or it has been defined (not null value) but it doesn’t contain any opening committee: if operation is called in RESET mode, all previously opening committees are removed, otherwise no operation is performed.
2. OpeningCommittee array contains at least one element: newly listed opening committees are inserted and, if operation is called in RESET mode, not listed opening committees are removed.
OpeningCommittee without CommitteeMembers will be rejected.
CommitteeMembers without CommitteeMember (user) will be rejected.
To add an opening committee the RfX must be the flag “Enable Opening Committees” enabled.

sections.title: RfX duplication
paragraphs: In case of creation of a new RfX from an existing RfX, system needs to know the RfX to inherit information from.
So, at least one between rfxIdFrom and rfxReferenceCodeFrom fields must be specified, must be not empty and must identify an existing RfX belonging to the same instance web service is called on.
When executing any other operation, these fields are ignored.

sections.title: Associated Master Item
paragraphs: When a master item is associated with an economical parameter, if the fields reference, unit of measure, goods group and notes relating to the parameter are not passed in the request, those relating to the master item will be taken.

sections.title: Change Owner User
paragraphs: When operation code CHANGE_OWNER is used, only owner user of the existing RfX will be updated. It’s necessary to provide the RfX identifier, rfxID or Reference Code, and new Owner User identifier. If assignOwnerDivision flag is set to true the RfX Division value will be set according to the Division of the new Owner.

sections.title: Update Attach Buyer
paragraphs: When operation code UPDATE_ATTACH_BUYER is used, only buyer side attachment of the existing RfX will be updated. It’s necessary to provide the RfX identifier, rfxID or Reference Code, and new Attachment. The attachment will be uploaded regardless the current status of the RfX.

sections.title: Rfx Technical Envelope Scoring
paragraphs: In section definitions the sectionPos is always preferred to the section name. A section is also known as a parameterGroup. The section name is not guaranteed to be unique. If a section position and a section name are given the section position will be used, even if the section name is not a valid section name. If a section name and a section name are given and both are not valid the webservice will respond with an appropriate error message.
In parameter definitions the parameter id is preferred.

sections.title: Additional Note:
paragraphs: The web service can always update all data in sections, even if they were copied from a template / have rules that can limit buyer updates to those template originated sections, because the web service runs as the GURU user and that user can always make updates to sections even if they were copied from a template and have rules limiting updates.

sections.title: Data Elements Condition Filters
paragraphs: A special filtering section named DEConditionFilter (Data Element Condition filter) can be specified in order to retrieve only rfx having data elements with specific values. If a data element condition filter is used, it will apply to either the RFX type data or the RFX Award type data, depending on how that data element is mapped. If a DE_ID is mapped to BOTH an RFX Type and an RFX Award Type, then filter will be applied to RFX type data.
A DEConditionFilter must specify:
1. Key: the name of the data element whose value must be matched
2. Operator: the kind of match required. The following operators can be applied:
3. EXIST, NOT_EXIST: data element has (hasn’t) been defined for the rfx

4. ISNULL, NOTNULL: data element value must (must not) be null (data element has been defined for the rfx and it hasn’t been answered –if ISNULL- or it has been answered no matter value –if NOTNULL-). Provided filter values are ignored
5. EQUAL, NOTEQUAL: data element value must (must not) match the first value in provided list
6. IN, NOT_IN: data element value must (must not) be found in provided list.
7. AT_LEAST_ONE: valid only for choice and multi choice typed data element, allow to ask data element value to match at least one of provided values (as string)
8. START_WITH, CONTAINS: valid only for textual data element, require data element value to begin with (to contain) first provided value
9. GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN: valid only for date and number typed data element, require data element value to be grater or equal (lower or equal) first provided value
10. Values: string representing the value to be filtered for. Depending on the target data element, it must be expressed in the following format:
11. TEXT: free text
12. NUMBER: string representing a number using dot to separate decimal
13. DATE: Date value expressed in the form “yyyy-MM-dd” (e.g. 2012-03-01) or “yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS Z” (e.g. 2012-03-01 12:36:42.535 +0100)
14. BOOLEAN: string “1”and “true” evaluate to TRUE, every other strings evaluate to FALSE
15. In case of option/multichoice data element, the value must be in the system default language. If the condition filter independentLocale is set, the value must be in the “neutral” language.
Attachment typed data elements allow the operators ISNULL, NOTNULL.
